hints: The number of subordinates of a manager is the size of their descendant subtree, excluding the manager.
Start at the leaves and pass each node's accumulated count upward to its parent.
A postorder traversal ensures children's counts are ready before the parent.
analogy: Each employee contributes one person plus everyone below them to their manager's total.
example: If employee 2 manages employees 4 and 5, they have two subordinates; their manager counts 2 plus all of 2's descendants.
algorithm: Run DFS from the root. Set size[u]=1+sum(size[child]); answer size[u]-1 for each non-root node.
correctness: The rooted tree's descendants are exactly the disjoint child subtrees; summing their sizes gives every subordinate once.
